notes:
CIRCUIT: a single-loop AC source circuit with a shunt branch. 16sin4t V source (V-AC #4) on the left rail; the top rail runs right through R#1 (4ohm) and C#0 (12F) to a mid node, then through L#2 (2H) to the right rail, which drops through R#3 (6ohm) to the bottom rail. From the mid node a vertical drops into a drawn rectangle whose left side is R#5 (2kohm) and whose right side is I-AC #6 (2cos4t A) - so those two are in PARALLEL between the mid node and the bottom rail. The bottom rail is the reference and carries GND #7. 8 components, 5 nets. (The big rectangle around the whole page at x~8..1015, y~273..745 is the scan's page border, not circuit wire; it forms its own isolated ink group with no terminals on it and does not affect any net.)

NET MAP:
  0  = BOTTOM RAIL / reference: bottom of V-AC #4, bottom of R#3 (6ohm), bottom of R#5 (2kohm), bottom of I-AC #6, and GND #7. The rectangle's bottom side, the stem down to the GND hatch, and the long horizontal at y~660 are all this one net (see S27/S29).
  n1 = short top-rail segment between R#1 (4ohm) right lead and C#0 (12F) left plate.
  n2 = MID NODE: right plate of C#0, left lead of L#2 (2H), plus the vertical at x~545 dropping from the top rail (site S0) to the top side of the rectangle (site S14), hence also the top of R#5 (2kohm) and the top of I-AC #6.
  n3 = LEFT RAIL TOP: top terminal of V-AC #4 up the left rail and right along the top wire to the left lead of R#1 (4ohm).
  n4 = RIGHT RAIL TOP: right lead of L#2 (2H) along the top wire to the top-right corner and down to the top of R#3 (6ohm).

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS:
  S0 (542,380) deg3 -> JUNCTION (agrees with default). Clean T: the top rail runs left-right and a single vertical stroke starts here and goes down. Nothing passes through; a T is unambiguously a junction. The alternative would orphan the vertical and leave the whole 2kohm / current-source branch with one floating end.
  S14 (547,466) deg3 -> JUNCTION (agrees with default). Clean T: the vertical from S0 comes down and lands on the top side of the drawn rectangle. Junction. If it were not joined, the 2kohm and the current source would have no connection at all to the rest of the circuit.
  S27 (553,600) deg3 -> JUNCTION (agrees with default). Clean T: the bottom side of the rectangle runs left-right and the stem to ground starts here going down. Junction.
  S29 (553,671) deg5 -> JUNCTION (matches the default, but this is the one genuinely load-bearing call on this sheet). Here the ground stem from S27 CROSSES the long bottom rail at y~671 and continues below it into the GND hatch symbol. It is a plain X: no solder dot (dot=1.4, i.e. ordinary stroke width) and no hop/jog (hop=0.0), so the ink alone does not settle it. Decided by electrical impossibility (rule 1): if this were a crossing, the bottom rail (V-AC bottom + 6ohm bottom) would be one net and the rectangle bottom (2kohm bottom + I-AC bottom + GND) a different net, which would leave the parallel 2kohm/current-source branch hanging off the mid node by a single connection - no return path, and a current source driving into an open. That is impossible, so the two must be joined. The junction reading also gives the physically expected result: the bottom rail IS the ground reference. Consequence recorded: the crossing reading would have produced 6 nets with a stranded 2-element branch.

NON-CRITICAL SITES (all left at default; every one of them is a stroke of a handwritten value label brushing a wire or a component body, and none changes the grouping): S1/S5 = '12F' label strokes touching the capacitor leads; S3/S4 = '2H' label touching the inductor's right lead; S8 = '4ohm' label under R#1; S15 = '6ohm' label touching R#3's body; S17/S18 = '2kohm' label touching R#5; S21/S22/S23/S24 = '2cos4t A' label strokes touching the I-AC symbol and its bottom lead.

PORT FIXES (all three are the 'terminal landed on the value label' failure; each showed up as a 1-terminal net):
  #0 Capacitor (12F): t1 was on p1@(423,407), a stroke of the '12F' caption below-left of the part - i.e. BOTH terminals were on the left side. Repointed t1 to p0@(474,381), the real right plate lead (wire 66) that runs right to site S0. This killed 1-terminal net n2 and put the capacitor's right plate on the mid node where it belongs.
  #1 Resistor (4ohm): t0 was on p1@(323,401), a stroke of the '4ohm' caption below the resistor. Repointed t0 to p2@(311,374), the real left lead (wire 188) that runs left to the top of the V-AC source. This merged the former 1-terminal nets n3 (resistor) and n7 (source top).
  #2 Inductor (2H): t1 was on p3@(677,405), a stroke of the '2H' caption below the coil. Repointed t1 to p4@(695,378), the real right lead (wire 211) that runs right to the top-right corner and down to R#3. This merged the former 1-terminal nets n5 (inductor) and n6 (6ohm top).
After these fixes every net has >= 2 terminals and the ERC is clean.

CLASSES: all eight labels match the drawn symbols (circle with a sine wave = V-AC; circle with a sine wave and an arrow through it = I-AC; three zigzags = Resistor; coil = Inductor; two parallel plates = Capacitor; hatch = GND). No reclassification, no unconnected leads, no gap bridges needed dropping.
